bull.b: A portfolio spanning five inherited retinal disease programs diversifies clinical risk and creates multiple opportunities for data, regulatory progress and eventual commercialization over the next several years.

First-mover positioning in specialized retinal diseases and access to rare-disease incentives could support differentiated development, faster regulatory pathways and stronger competitive protection if clinical results are successful.

Stated funding visibility through 2029 would allow Opus to pursue several programs and reach planned clinical milestones without immediate operational disruption, potentially preserving the value of upcoming data readouts.

bear.b: Extremely deep operating and net losses indicate that current revenue is insufficient to support the business, leaving future progress dependent on successful development, major cost control or additional financing.

Negative equity combined with new debt weakens financial flexibility and may constrain financing options, especially while the company remains loss-making and requires substantial investment in clinical development.

Sustained and worsening cash consumption means Opus relies on external funding to maintain operations, creating dilution or liquidity risk if clinical spending continues before products generate meaningful revenue.
